second_integration.review: PR36 stores one exact OHLCV scalar snapshot and invalidates event caches after in-place input changes. Complete prior behavior and tape-consumer tests remain. This does not qualify the underlying pattern classifier.

repairs: General native warehouse histories retain full received packet/obs rows, strict finite signed/zero scalars, strict normalized days, explicit exclusions, duplicate conflicts and source metadata.

Full native id matching is case-insensitive without suffix/provider substitution. Existing explicit aliases retain requested and canonical identities. Named exchanges cannot inherit an unqualified macro alias.
Initial URL loading preserves scalar identifier spelling. Classification avoids recursion through the market ticker resolver. Missing observation modules do not permit market fallbacks.

Eight LRU packet caches share bounded deadlines, recheck/backoff, pending promise deduplication and reset-generation guards. Eviction aborts pending downloads; late bodies cannot restore evicted state.
Failed replacements retain the prior accepted packet with visible failure and the complete decoded rejected replacement. An initial rejection remains unavailable with its evidence.
Scalar histories no longer accumulate strong whole-packet references across intervals in the unused market bar cache. Scalar display disables price/trading calculations.
Received normalized days and packet construction time are labeled explicitly; upstream original precision, acquisition, publication and provider equivalence remain unverified.
review_followups: The first dedicated candidate regressions failed 11 of 16 cases: row dispatch did not yet include warehouse rows and classification recursed through equity resolution. Both were corrected before the final successful focused/browser/full runs.

An offline initial URL case exposed legacy identifier uppercasing. Complete invented failure state is retained; initial scalar spelling is now preserved. Unrelated initialization is checked by an exact single-statement replacement.

The first full frontend run found six missing-window failures in a legacy isolated detail harness. Its full predecessor and every assertion are retained; the harness now includes the real resolver and browser-global context, without changing product code.
Sparse custom source-path arrays are rejected. Existing seven default observation sources and previous tests remain preserved.
Visual review confirms signed scalar plots and visible failure/source panels. Existing floating-point axis noise, gap-bridging lines and crowded legacy mobile chrome remain separately open.

Incoming PR34 diagnostics preserve closed policy and add fixed explanations; fifteen native cases pass. Incoming PR35 counterexamples are retained, but production volume calculations remain unqualified.
